# Holepunch GitHub Actions

[`holepunchto/actions`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions) is a collection of reusable composite GitHub Actions for building, signing, publishing, and recovering Pear applications and Holepunch modules. Reference one with:

```yaml
- uses: holepunchto/actions/<name>@v1
```

There is no project-scaffolding action. To bootstrap a new Pear project, clone the [`hello-pear-electron`](https://github.com/holepunchto/hello-pear-electron) template. The actions below automate CI/CD once a project exists.

## Pear app CI/CD

| Action | Purpose | Key inputs / outputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`make-pear-app`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/make-pear-app) | Run `npm run make` for the host OS with code signing and notarization, then upload distributables as artifacts. Handles its own `setup-node` + `npm ci`; precede it with `actions/checkout@v4`. See [Build and sign desktop apps in CI](/how-to/operate-an-app/github-actions/build-and-sign-in-ci). | In: `channel` (required), `upgrade_key`, macOS signing/notarization (`macos_certificate_base64`, `macos_p12_password`, `macos_codesign_identity`, `macos_notarization_method` = `appstore_connect` \| `apple_id_password`, plus the matching API-key or Apple-ID fields), Windows signing (`windows_signing_method` = `windows_cert_sha1` \| `windows_cert_pfx`, plus cert fields), `linux_set_up_snapcraft`. Out: `artifact-links` |
| [`pear-ci`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/pear-ci) | Stage a directory into a [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) on every run, producing a stable `pear://` link. Documented in full at [pear-ci GitHub Action](/reference/ci-and-release/pear-ci-action). | `primary-key`, `namespace`, `target`, `dry-run`; out: `pr-url` |
| [`pear-provision-recover`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/pear-provision-recover) | Recover a provision drive from the network into a new writable drive (runs the `pear-provision-recover` CLI). Used to rebuild write access—see [Recovering from lost write access](/how-to/operate-an-app/manual-deployment/troubleshoot-desktop-releases#recovering-from-lost-write-access). | `path`, `key`, `length`, `blobs-length`, `primary-key`, `name` (all required) |

## Release

| Action | Purpose | Key inputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`publish`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/publish) | `npm publish` (honoring dist-tag and workspaces) then create a GitHub release via `create-release`. | `tag` (default `latest`), `workspaces`, `include-workspace-root`, `node-auth-token` |
| [`create-release`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/create-release) | `npm pack` the packages and attach the tarballs to a `gh release create` for the current ref. | `workspaces`, `include-workspace-root` |
| [`trigger-canary`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/trigger-canary) | Dispatch a `release` event to the `holepunchto/canary-tests` repo so downstream canary tests run against a new release. | `repository`, `ref`, `token` (all required) |

## Bare native-addon prebuilds

For authors of native [Bare](/reference/modules/bare-modules) addons who build prebuilt binaries across platforms in CI. The typical shape is a build matrix where each job runs `compile-prebuilds`, then a final job merges the per-platform artifacts.

| Action | Purpose | Key inputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`compile-prebuilds`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/compile-prebuilds) | Install `bare-make`, then `generate` / `build` / `install` a native prebuild for one platform + arch, optionally uploading it. | `platform` (required), `arch` (required), `flags`, `tags`, `prefix` (default `prebuilds`), `upload` |
| [`upload-prebuilds`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/upload-prebuilds) | Upload a compiled prebuild as an artifact named `<platform>-<arch><tags>`. | `platform` (required), `arch` (required), `tags`, `prefix` |
| [`download-prebuilds`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/download-prebuilds) | Download all prebuild artifacts into one directory (`merge-multiple`). | `prefix` (default `prebuilds`) |
| [`merge-prebuilds`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/merge-prebuilds) | Download every per-platform prebuild artifact and re-upload them as a single `prebuilds` artifact. |—|

### Project and toolchain setup

These are the building blocks the prebuild and release actions compose; you can also use them directly.

| Action | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`checkout`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/checkout) | `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false`. |
| [`setup-node`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-node) | Install Node.js LTS and configure the npm registry/scope for auth. |
| [`node-base`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/node-base) | `checkout` + `setup-node` + `npm install` (with `allow-git`, `force-install`, registry/scope/auth options). |
| [`setup-bare`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-bare) | Install the `bare-runtime` globally. |
| [`bare-base`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/bare-base) | `node-base` + `setup-bare`: configure a Bare project on a runner. |
| [`setup-llvm`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-llvm), [`setup-nasm`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-nasm), [`setup-swift`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-swift), [`swift-base`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/swift-base) | Install the compilers and toolchains (LLVM, NASM, Swift) used when compiling native prebuilds and platform-specific code. |
| [`setup-socket`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-socket), [`setup-mininet`](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/tree/main/setup-mininet) | Install supporting tooling: `setup-socket` configures Socket.dev supply-chain scanning; `setup-mininet` installs Mininet and Open vSwitch for network-emulation tests. |

## See also

- [Build and sign desktop apps in CI](/how-to/operate-an-app/github-actions/build-and-sign-in-ci)—the `make-pear-app` walkthrough.
- [Publish with GitHub Actions](/how-to/operate-an-app/github-actions/publish-with-github-actions) and [pear-ci GitHub Action](/reference/ci-and-release/pear-ci-action)—staging with `pear-ci`.
- [Build desktop distributables](/how-to/operate-an-app/build-and-package/build-desktop-distributables)—the manual signing flow `make-pear-app` automates.
- [Bare modules](/reference/modules/bare-modules)—the runtime the prebuild pipeline targets.

# pear-ci GitHub Action

The [`pear-ci` GitHub Action](https://github.com/holepunchto/actions/blob/main/pear-ci/action.yml) stages a directory from your repository into a [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) on every run, producing a stable `pear://` link your app can use as its [`upgrade`](/reference/pear/configuration) field. For the task-oriented setup, see [Publish with GitHub Actions](/how-to/operate-an-app/github-actions/publish-with-github-actions).

It is a composite action that installs the [`pear-ci`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pear-ci) npm tool, fetches the committed snapshot from `main`, stages, and commits the updated snapshot back.

## Usage

```yaml
- uses: holepunchto/actions/pear-ci@main
  with:
    primary-key: ${{ secrets.PEAR_PRIMARY_KEY }}
    namespace: my-app
    target: dist
    dry-run: false
```

## Inputs

| Input | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary-key` | Yes |—| 32-byte (64 hex character) key for the [Corestore](/reference/helpers/corestore) identity. Determines the drive's `pear://` link across runs. Store it as a secret. |
| `namespace` | Yes |—| Drive namespace name. Combined with `primary-key` to derive the drive. Only letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, and underscores. |
| `target` | Yes |—| Repo-relative path of the directory to stage. Must not be absolute or contain `..`. |
| `dry-run` | No | `false` | When `true`, computes and logs the diff without writing to the drive or committing the snapshot. Must be `true` or `false`. |
| `github-token` | No | `${{ github.token }}` | Token used to fetch and commit `ci/snapshot.json`. |
| `app-slug` | No |—| When set, the snapshot commit is attributed to the matching GitHub App bot identity instead of `github-actions[bot]`. |

## Outputs

| Output | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pr-url` | URL of the PR created if a direct push of the snapshot to `main` failed; empty otherwise. |

## Input validation

The action rejects malformed inputs before staging:

- `primary-key` must match `^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$`.
- `namespace` must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`.
- `target` must contain only `[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]`, must not be an absolute path, and must not contain `..` (no directory traversal).
- `dry-run` must be exactly `true` or `false`.

## Snapshot commits

The action reads `ci/snapshot.json` from `main` before staging and writes it back afterward. The snapshot records each core's length so subsequent runs sync only what changed. When `dry-run` is `true`, no commit is made. If pushing the snapshot directly to `main` fails, the action pushes a `pear-ci/snapshot-<run-id>` branch and opens a PR, exposing its URL via the `pr-url` output.

Grant the workflow `contents: write` (and `pull-requests: write` if you want the PR fallback) so the snapshot commit can land.

## Underlying CLI

Outside of Actions, the same staging runs through the [`pear-ci`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pear-ci) CLI:

```bash
npm install -g pear-ci
pear-ci \
  --primary-key <64-hex-key> \
  --name my-app \
  --target ./dist \
  --snapshot ci/snapshot.json \
  --storage /tmp/store
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--primary-key` | 32-byte hex key for the [Corestore](/reference/helpers/corestore). |
| `--name` | Namespace name used to derive the drive. |
| `--target` | Local directory to mirror into the drive. |
| `--snapshot` | Path to read/write the JSON snapshot. |
| `--storage` | Corestore storage path. |
| `--dry-run` | Compute the diff without writing to the drive. |

The CLI logs the drive key it stages to (`starting stage for key <drive-key>`)—that key is your `pear://` link. See the [`pear-ci` README](https://github.com/holepunchto/pear-ci#readme) for the programmatic API and snapshot format.

## See also

- [Publish with GitHub Actions](/how-to/operate-an-app/github-actions/publish-with-github-actions)—step-by-step setup.
- [Holepunch GitHub Actions](/reference/ci-and-release/github-actions)—the full catalog of shared actions this is part of.
- [Configuration](/reference/pear/configuration)—the `upgrade` field this link feeds.
- [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) and [Hyperswarm](/reference/building-blocks/hyperswarm)—the building blocks `pear-ci` stages and replicates over.
- [Deploy your application](/how-to/operate-an-app/manual-deployment/deployment)—the manual staging flow.

# compact-encoding

`compact-encoding` packages small binary codecs behind a shared encoder interface. It is commonly paired with [Protomux](/reference/helpers/protomux) message schemas and shows up in [Hypercore](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore) and other Holepunch protocol surfaces whenever structured binary payloads matter. For the upstream package and implementation details, see the [compact-encoding repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding).

## Module-level encode and decode helpers

#### `const buffer = cenc.encode(enc, value)`

Encodes a single `value` using `enc` into a freshly allocated `Buffer` and returns it. Equivalent to manually creating a state, calling `enc.preencode` and `enc.encode`, and slicing the buffer — useful when you just want bytes back in one step.

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enc` | `object` | Any compact-encoding encoder (for example `cenc.uint`, a custom encoder). |
| `value` | `*` | The value to encode. |

- Returns: `Buffer`

```js
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.uint, 42)
// <Buffer 2a>
```

#### `const value = cenc.decode(enc, buffer)`

Decodes a single value from `buffer` using `enc`. Equivalent to constructing a state from the buffer and calling `enc.decode`.

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enc` | `object` | Any compact-encoding encoder. |
| `buffer` | `Buffer` | The buffer to decode from. |

- Returns: The decoded value.

```js
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.uint, buf) // 42
```

## Install

```sh
npm i compact-encoding
```

## Quickstart

```js
import cenc from 'compact-encoding'

const state = cenc.state()

cenc.uint.preencode(state, 42)
cenc.string.preencode(state, 'hello')

state.buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(state.end)
state.start = 0

cenc.uint.encode(state, 42)
cenc.string.encode(state, 'hello')

state.start = 0

console.log(cenc.uint.decode(state))
console.log(cenc.string.decode(state))
```

## API Reference

### Encoder contract

Every bundled encoder follows the same three-method contract. The top-level helpers and exported factories below all return or consume objects with this shape.

#### `enc.preencode(state, val)`

Does a fast preencode dry-run that only sets state.end. Use this to figure out how big of a buffer you need.

#### `enc.encode(state, val)`

Writes the encoded form of the value into `state.buffer` at `state.start` (the buffer must have been preallocated via `preencode`), advancing `state.start` past the written bytes.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `object` | A compact-encoding state with `start`, `end`, and `buffer`. |
| `val` | `*` | The value to encode. |

- Returns: `undefined` — the encoded bytes are written into `state.buffer` in place.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const state = cenc.state()
cenc.uint.preencode(state, 42)
state.buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(state.end)
cenc.uint.encode(state, 42)
// state.buffer is a 1-byte Buffer containing the encoded uint
```

#### `val = enc.decode(state)`

Reads and returns a value from `state.buffer` at `state.start`, advancing `state.start` past the decoded value.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `object` | A compact-encoding state with `start`, `end`, and `buffer`. |

- Returns: `*` — The decoded value.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.bool, true)
const state = cenc.state(0, buf.byteLength, buf)
const val = cenc.bool.decode(state) // true
```

### State and convenience helpers

#### `cenc.state(start = 0, end = 0, buffer = null)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L5)

A mutable state object `{ start, end, buffer }` used by all encoders.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | `number` | `0` | Initial read/write offset. |
| `end` | `number` | `0` | Initial end offset (set by preencode to determine required buffer size). |
| `buffer` | [`Buffer\|Uint8Array\|null`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | `null` | Underlying buffer; allocate after preencoding. |

- Returns: [`State`](#state) — A new state object `{ start, end, buffer }`.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const state = cenc.state()
cenc.uint.preencode(state, 42)
cenc.string.preencode(state, 'hi')
state.buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(state.end)
cenc.uint.encode(state, 42)
cenc.string.encode(state, 'hi')
```

#### `cenc.from(enc)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L966)

Coerces `enc` — an existing compact encoder, a named raw string encoding such as `'utf8'` or `'json'`, a codec with `encode`/`decode`, or an abstract encoding with `encodingLength` — into a compact-encoding-compatible encoder object.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enc` | `string\|object` | An encoding name, compact encoder, abstract-encoding, or codec. |

- Returns: `object` — A compact-encoding encoder with `preencode`, `encode`, and `decode`.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const enc = cenc.from('utf-8')
const buf = cenc.encode(enc, 'hello')
const val = cenc.decode(enc, buf) // 'hello'
```

### Encoder factories

#### `cenc.fixed(n)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L526)

An encoder for fixed-size buffers, where `n` is the exact byte length every encoded value must have.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n` | `number` | Exact number of bytes to encode/decode. |

- Returns: `object` — An encoder that reads and writes exactly `n` bytes.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const enc = cenc.fixed(4)
const buf = cenc.encode(enc, Buffer.alloc(4, 0xff))
const val = cenc.decode(enc, buf) // <Buffer ff ff ff ff>
```

#### `cenc.array(enc)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L546)

An encoder that prefixes arrays with their length and encodes each item in order using `enc`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enc` | `object` | An encoder with `preencode`, `encode`, and `decode` methods. |

- Returns: `object` — An encoder for arrays of values handled by `enc`.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const enc = cenc.array(cenc.uint)
const buf = cenc.encode(enc, [1, 2, 3])
const val = cenc.decode(enc, buf) // [1, 2, 3]
```

#### `cenc.frame(enc)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L566)

An encoder that prefixes one encoded payload with its byte length.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enc` | `object` | An encoder with `preencode`, `encode`, and `decode` methods. |

- Returns: `object` — An encoder that wraps each value in a byte-length frame.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const enc = cenc.frame(cenc.string)
const buf = cenc.encode(enc, 'hello')
const val = cenc.decode(enc, buf) // 'hello'
```

#### `cenc.record(keyEncoding, valueEncoding)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L919)

An encoder for plain object records, with `keyEncoding` for object keys and `valueEncoding` for object values.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyEncoding` | `object` | Encoder used for each object key. |
| `valueEncoding` | `object` | Encoder used for each object value. |

- Returns: `object` — An encoder that reads/writes plain objects as key-value pairs.

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const enc = cenc.record(cenc.string, cenc.uint)
const buf = cenc.encode(enc, { a: 1, b: 2 })
const val = cenc.decode(enc, buf) // [Object: null prototype] { a: 1, b: 2 }
```

#### `cenc.stringRecord`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L948)

A prebuilt `record(cenc.string, cenc.string)` encoder for simple string maps.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.stringRecord, { name: 'alice', role: 'admin' })
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.stringRecord, buf) // [Object: null prototype] { name: 'alice', role: 'admin' }
```

### Numeric encodings

#### `cenc.uint64`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L180)

Unsigned integer encoders (`cenc.uint`, `cenc.uint8`, `cenc.uint16`, `cenc.uint24`, `cenc.uint32`, `cenc.uint40`, `cenc.uint48`, `cenc.uint56`, `cenc.uint64`). `cenc.uint` chooses a compact size automatically; the fixed-width variants always use the named byte width.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.uint64, 2 ** 32)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.uint64, buf) // 4294967296
```

#### `cenc.int64`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L224)

Signed integer encoders (`cenc.int`, `cenc.int8` … `cenc.int64`) built on top of the unsigned variants with ZigZag encoding.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.int64, -4294967296)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.int64, buf) // -4294967296
```

#### `cenc.bigint`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L291)

BigInt-aware integer encoders (`cenc.biguint64`, `cenc.bigint64`, `cenc.biguint`, `cenc.bigint`) for fixed-width or variable-width large integer values.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.bigint, -(2n ** 128n))
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.bigint, buf) // -340282366920938463463374607431768211456n
```

#### `cenc.float64`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L321)

Floating-point encoders (`cenc.float32`, `cenc.float64`) using IEEE-754 little-endian layouts.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.float64, Math.PI)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.float64, buf) // 3.141592653589793
```

#### `cenc.lexint`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L293)

The lexicographic integer encoder exported from the `./lexint` module.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.lexint, 1000)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.lexint, buf) // 1000
```

### Binary, buffer, and typed-array encodings

#### `cenc.binary`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L378)

Buffer-oriented encoders. `buffer` length-prefixes a byte sequence, `optionalBuffer` maps zero length to `null`, and `binary` accepts either a string or buffer-like input.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.binary, 'hello')
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.binary, buf) // <Buffer 68 65 6c 6c 6f>
```

#### `cenc.arraybuffer`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L390)

An encoder for `ArrayBuffer` instances.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const ab = new ArrayBuffer(4)
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.arraybuffer, ab)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.arraybuffer, buf) // ArrayBuffer { byteLength: 4 }
```

#### `cenc.float64array`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L459)

Length-prefixed typed-array encoders (`cenc.uint8array`, `cenc.uint16array`, `cenc.uint32array`, `cenc.int8array`, `cenc.int16array`, `cenc.int32array`, `cenc.biguint64array`, `cenc.bigint64array`, `cenc.float32array`, `cenc.float64array`) that preserve the underlying element type.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.float64array, new Float64Array([Math.PI]))
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.float64array, buf) // Float64Array [3.141592653589793]
```

#### `cenc.fixed64`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L544)

Prebuilt fixed-size buffer encoders (`cenc.fixed32`, `cenc.fixed64`) for 32-byte and 64-byte values.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const sig = Buffer.alloc(64)
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.fixed64, sig)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.fixed64, buf) // <Buffer 00 00 ... (64 bytes)>
```

### Text encodings

#### `cenc.ucs2`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L511)

String encoders for the named text encoding (`cenc.string`, `cenc.utf8`, `cenc.ascii`, `cenc.hex`, `cenc.base64`, `cenc.utf16le`, `cenc.ucs2`). Each one also exposes `.fixed(length)` for fixed-size strings.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.ucs2, 'hi')
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.ucs2, buf) // 'hi'
```

### Boolean, date, and structured-value encodings

#### `cenc.bool`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L513)

A one-byte boolean encoder.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.bool, true)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.bool, buf) // true
```

#### `cenc.date`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L593)

A `Date` encoder backed by the signed integer timestamp value from `date.getTime()`.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.date, new Date('2024-01-01'))
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.date, buf) // Date object for 2024-01-01
```

#### `cenc.ndjson`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L617)

UTF-8 JSON encoders (`cenc.json`, `cenc.ndjson`). `ndjson` appends a trailing newline before encoding.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.ndjson, { a: 1 })
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.ndjson, buf) // { a: 1 }
```

#### `cenc.none`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L630)

A sentinel encoder that always decodes to `null` and writes no payload bytes.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.none, null)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.none, buf) // null
```

#### `cenc.any`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L708)

A schemaless tagged-value encoder for JSON-like values, arrays, objects, dates, strings, buffers, booleans, integers, and floats.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.any, { n: 42, flag: true })
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.any, buf) // { n: 42, flag: true }
```

### Network encodings

#### `cenc.port`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L726)

The same encoder as `cenc.uint16`, provided for protocol readability when encoding network ports.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.port, 8080)
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.port, buf) // 8080
```

#### `cenc.ip`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L880)

Encoders for IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, or either family with an embedded family tag (`cenc.ipv4`, `cenc.ipv6`, `cenc.ip`).

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf4 = cenc.encode(cenc.ip, '1.2.3.4')
cenc.decode(cenc.ip, buf4) // '1.2.3.4'
const buf6 = cenc.encode(cenc.ip, '::1')
cenc.decode(cenc.ip, buf6) // '0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1'
```

#### `cenc.ipAddress`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L900)

Address-object encoders (`cenc.ipv4Address`, `cenc.ipv6Address`, `cenc.ipAddress`) for `{ host, family?, port }` shapes.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
const buf = cenc.encode(cenc.ipAddress, { host: '1.2.3.4', port: 8080 })
const val = cenc.decode(cenc.ipAddress, buf) // { host: '1.2.3.4', family: 4, port: 8080 }
```

### Raw variants

#### `cenc.raw`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding/blob/v3.3.0/index.js#L9)

A namespace of non-length-prefixed variants for many buffer, string, array, JSON, and typed-array encodings such as `cenc.raw.buffer`, `cenc.raw.utf8`, `cenc.raw.array(enc)`, and `cenc.raw.json`.

- Returns: `object`

```js
const cenc = require('compact-encoding')
// copy raw bytes into state
const buf = Buffer.from([1, 2, 3])
const state = cenc.state()
cenc.raw.preencode(state, buf)
state.buffer = Buffer.allocUnsafe(state.end)
cenc.raw.encode(state, buf)
```

### Complete codec reference

The sections above detail the contract and the most common encoders. Below is the full catalog of bundled codecs shipped by compact-encoding v3.3.0. Every entry is an object implementing the [encoder contract](#encoder-contract) (`preencode` / `encode` / `decode`), so any of them can be composed with [`cenc.array(enc)`](#cencarrayenc), [`cenc.frame(enc)`](#cencframeenc), or used directly with [`cenc.encode`](#const-buffer--cencencodeenc-value) / [`cenc.decode`](#const-value--cencdecodeenc-buffer). Fixed-size integers are little-endian unless the name ends in `be`.

**Unsigned integers**

| Codec | Bytes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cenc.uint` | 1–9 | Smallest fixed-size encoding with a prefix signalling which; best for values spanning a wide range. |
| `cenc.uint8` | 1 | Fixed `uint8`. |
| `cenc.uint16` | 2 | Fixed `uint16`; useful for ports. |
| `cenc.uint24` | 3 | Fixed `uint24`; useful for message framing. |
| `cenc.uint32` | 4 | Fixed `uint32`; useful for large message framing. |
| `cenc.uint32be` | 4 | Big-endian `uint32`. |
| `cenc.uint40` | 5 | Fixed `uint40`. |
| `cenc.uint48` | 6 | Fixed `uint48`. |
| `cenc.uint56` | 7 | Fixed `uint56`. |
| `cenc.uint64` | 8 | Fixed `uint64`. |
| `cenc.uint64be` | 8 | Big-endian `uint64`. |

**Signed integers** — each is the matching unsigned codec with [ZigZag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variable-length_quantity#Zigzag_encoding) encoding, so small-magnitude negatives stay compact.

| Codec | Bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.int` | 1–9 |
| `cenc.int8` | 1 |
| `cenc.int16` | 2 |
| `cenc.int24` | 3 |
| `cenc.int32` | 4 |
| `cenc.int40` | 5 |
| `cenc.int48` | 6 |
| `cenc.int56` | 7 |
| `cenc.int64` | 8 |

**Big integers**

| Codec | Bytes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cenc.biguint64` | 8 | Fixed `biguint64`. |
| `cenc.bigint64` | 8 | `biguint64` with ZigZag encoding. |
| `cenc.biguint` | variable | Word count `uint`-prefixed. |
| `cenc.bigint` | variable | `biguint` with ZigZag encoding. |

**Floating point**

| Codec | Bytes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.float32` | 4 |
| `cenc.float64` | 8 |

**Buffers**

| Codec | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.buffer` | Buffer with a `uint` length prefix. |
| `cenc.optionalBuffer` | Like `cenc.buffer` but round-trips `null`/absent values. |
| `cenc.binary` | Buffer or string, length-prefixed; decodes to a buffer. |
| `cenc.arraybuffer` | `ArrayBuffer` with a `uint` length prefix. |

**Typed arrays** — each is prefixed with its element count as a `uint`.

| Codec | Element type |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.uint8array` | `Uint8Array` |
| `cenc.uint16array` | `Uint16Array` |
| `cenc.uint32array` | `Uint32Array` |
| `cenc.int8array` | `Int8Array` |
| `cenc.int16array` | `Int16Array` |
| `cenc.int32array` | `Int32Array` |
| `cenc.biguint64array` | `BigUint64Array` |
| `cenc.bigint64array` | `BigInt64Array` |
| `cenc.float32array` | `Float32Array` |
| `cenc.float64array` | `Float64Array` |

**Strings** — each is length-prefixed and also exposes a `.fixed(n)` factory for a fixed-length variant (for example `cenc.hex.fixed(32)`).

| Codec | Encoding |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.string`, `cenc.utf8` | UTF-8 |
| `cenc.ascii` | ASCII |
| `cenc.hex` | Hex |
| `cenc.base64` | Base64 |
| `cenc.utf16le`, `cenc.ucs2` | UTF-16LE |

**Fixed-size buffers**

| Codec | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.fixed(n)` | Factory for an `n`-byte fixed buffer (no length prefix). |
| `cenc.fixed32` | Fixed 32-byte buffer. |
| `cenc.fixed64` | Fixed 64-byte buffer. |

**Structured & special values**

| Codec | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.bool` | Encodes a boolean as `1` or `0`. |
| `cenc.date` | Encodes a `Date`. |
| `cenc.json` | JSON value serialized as UTF-8. |
| `cenc.ndjson` | JSON value serialized as newline-delimited UTF-8. |
| `cenc.any` | Any JSON-representable value into a self-describing buffer (compact types); useful for schemaless codecs. |
| `cenc.none` | Encodes nothing—placeholder for empty fields. |
| `cenc.array(enc)` | Length-prefixed array of `enc` values. |
| `cenc.frame(enc)` | Wraps `enc` with a `uint` byte-length frame prefix. |
| `cenc.record(keyEnc, valueEnc)` | Length-prefixed map of key/value pairs. |
| `cenc.stringRecord` | `record(utf8, utf8)`—a string-to-string map. |

**Network addresses**

| Codec | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `cenc.port` | Port number (alias of `cenc.uint16`). |
| `cenc.ipv4` | IPv4 address. |
| `cenc.ipv4Address` | IPv4 address plus port. |
| `cenc.ipv6` | IPv6 address. |
| `cenc.ipv6Address` | IPv6 address plus port. |
| `cenc.ip` | Dual IPv4/IPv6 address. |
| `cenc.ipAddress` | Dual IPv4/IPv6 address plus port. |

**Non-prefixed variants** — [`cenc.raw`](#cencraw) exposes length-prefix-free versions of the buffer, string, typed-array, array, and JSON codecs: `cenc.raw.buffer`, `cenc.raw.arraybuffer`, `cenc.raw.<typedarray>`, `cenc.raw.utf8` / `cenc.raw.ascii` / `cenc.raw.hex` / `cenc.raw.base64` / `cenc.raw.ucs2`, `cenc.raw.array(enc)`, `cenc.raw.json`, and `cenc.raw.ndjson`.

## Types

### State

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | `number` | — | Byte offset to read/write from. Advances after each encode/decode call. |
| `end` | `number` | — | Byte offset marking the end of valid data. Advances during preencode. |
| `buffer` | [`Buffer\|Uint8Array\|null`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | — | The underlying byte buffer. Set to `null` until allocation. |

## See also

- [Protomux](/reference/helpers/protomux)—the most common higher-level protocol surface built directly on compact-encoding schemas.
- [Hypercore](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore)—accepts compact encodings for structured values and message payloads.
- [Upstream compact-encoding repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/compact-encoding)—source, releases, and implementation details.

/reference/helpers/corestore/.markdown:
# Corestore

`Corestore` manages many related [Hypercores](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore) behind one storage root and one replication surface. It is the helper you usually share across [Hyperbee](/reference/building-blocks/hyperbee), [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive), and [Autobase](/reference/building-blocks/autobase) instances. For upstream source and changelog context, see the [Corestore repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore).

## Install

```sh
npm i corestore
```

## Quickstart

```js
import Corestore from 'corestore'

const store = new Corestore('./app-storage')
await store.ready()

const messages = store.get({
  name: 'messages',
  valueEncoding: 'json'
})

await messages.ready()
await messages.append({ text: 'hello from corestore' })

console.log(await messages.get(0))

await store.close()
```

## API Reference

### Constructor and lifecycle

#### `new Corestore(storage, options = {})`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L205)

Create a new Corestore instance.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storage` | `string\|object` | — | can be either a `hypercore-storage` instance or a string. |
| `options` | [`CorestoreOptions`](#corestoreoptions) | `{}` | Store options. |

- Throws: `ERR_ASSERTION` if `primaryKey` is set on a root store without `unsafe: true`.

#### `await store.ready()`

A promise that resolves once the storage seed is loaded and properties such as `store.primaryKey` are available.

#### `await store.close()`

Fully close this Corestore instance.

#### `await store.suspend([options])`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L351)

Suspend the underlying storage for the Corestore.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `object` | `{}` | Suspend options. |

- Returns: [`Promise<void>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves once the storage is flushed and suspended.

```js
await store.suspend()
```

#### `await store.resume()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L358)

Resume a suspended Corestore.

- Returns: [`Promise<void>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves once the storage is resumed.

```js
await store.resume()
```

### Store properties

#### `store.storage`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L240)

The backing storage adapter used for aliases, seeds, and Hypercore data files.

- Returns: `object`

#### `store.primaryKey`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L255)

The 32-byte primary key used to deterministically derive writable named cores and namespaced key pairs.

- Returns: [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer)

#### `store.readOnly`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L253)

`true` when the store was opened without write access.

- Returns: `boolean`

#### `store.manifestVersion`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L257)

The Hypercore manifest version used when Corestore creates new writable cores.

- Returns: `number`

#### `store.active`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L259)

`true` when the store should automatically attach loaded cores to active replication streams.

- Returns: `boolean`

#### `store.opened` / `store.closed`

`true` once [`store.ready()`](#await-storeready) has resolved / once [`store.close()`](#await-storeclose) has completed. Useful for guarding access to a store whose lifecycle you don't fully control.

- Returns: `boolean`

### Loading cores and scoping sessions

#### `store.get(key | { name: 'a-name', ...hypercoreOpts})`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L559)

Loads a Hypercore, either by name (if the `name` option is provided), or from the provided key (if the first argument is a Buffer or String with hex/z32 key, or if the `key` options is set).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | [`Buffer\|string\|object`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | A key (Buffer/hex/z32 string), or an options object with `name`, `key`, or `discoveryKey` plus Hypercore options. |

- Returns: [`Hypercore`](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore) — A Hypercore session for the requested core.

```js
const core = store.get({ name: 'my-core' })
```

#### `storeA.session()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.11.0/index.js#L367)

Create a new Corestore session. Closing a session will close all cores made from this session.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `object` | Session options (forwarded to the new Corestore). |

- Returns: [`Corestore`](/reference/helpers/corestore) — A new Corestore session sharing the same storage.

```js
const session = store.session()
```

#### `store.namespace(name)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L372)

Create a new namespaced Corestore session. Namespacing is useful if you're going to be sharing a single Corestore instance between many applications or components, as it prevents name collisions.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | [`string\|Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | Namespace name; combined with the current namespace to derive a new one. |
| `opts` | `object` | Session options (forwarded to the new Corestore). |

- Returns: [`Corestore`](/reference/helpers/corestore) — A new namespaced Corestore session.

```js
const ns1 = store.namespace('a')
const ns2 = ns1.namespace('b')
const core1 = ns1.get({ name: 'main' }) // These will load different Hypercores
const core2 = ns2.get({ name: 'main' })
```

### Replication and discovery

#### `store.replicate(optsOrStream)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L476)

Creates a replication stream that's capable of replicating all Hypercores that are managed by the Corestore, assuming the remote peer has the correct capabilities.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isInitiator` | [`boolean\|Stream`](https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html) | `true`/`false` to initiate, or an existing stream/connection to replicate over. |
| `opts` | `object` | Replication options, forwarded to the protocol stream. |

- Returns: [`Stream`](https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html) — The replication stream.

```js
const swarm = new Hyperswarm()

// join the relevant topic
swarm.join(...)

// simply pass the connection stream to corestore
swarm.on('connection', (connection) => store.replicate(connection))
```

#### `store.findingPeers()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L336)

A completion callback. Call it after the current peer-discovery pass finishes so pending update waits on loaded cores can unblock.

- Returns: `Function` — A `done` function to call once peer discovery has finished.

```js
const done = store.findingPeers()
swarm.flush().then(done, done)
```

#### `store.list(namespace)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L379)

Creates a discovery key stream of all cores within a namespace or all cores in general if no namespace is provided.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `namespace` | [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | to scope to; omit to list all cores. |

- Returns: [`Readable`](https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html#class-streamreadable) — A stream of discovery keys.

```js
for await (const discoveryKey of store.list()) console.log(discoveryKey)
```

#### `store.getAuth(discoveryKey)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L383)

The storage-layer auth metadata for that core, including manifest details when available.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `discoveryKey` | [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | Discovery key of the core to look up. |

- Returns: [`Promise<object\|null>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — The auth record, or `null` if not stored.

```js
const auth = await store.getAuth(discoveryKey)
```

### Key derivation and maintenance

#### `await store.createKeyPair(name, ns = this.ns)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L616)

Generate a key pair seeded with the Corestore's primary key using a `name` and a `ns` aka namespace. `ns` defaults to the current namespace.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | to derive the key pair from. |
| `ns` | [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | `this.ns` | — |

- Returns: [`Promise<{publicKey: Buffer, secretKey: Buffer}>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — The derived key pair.

```js
const keyPair = await store.createKeyPair('signer')
```

#### `store.audit(opts = {})`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L347)

An audit report describing the state of the backing store and any detected inconsistencies.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `object` | `{}` | Audit options (for example `dryRun`). |

- Returns: `AsyncGenerator<object>` — Yields a result per core as it is audited.

```js
for await (const report of store.audit()) console.log(report)
```

#### `await store.staticify(core, opts)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L515)

A reopened Hypercore whose manifest is converted into a static prologue-based manifest for the current data snapshot.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | [`Hypercore`](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore) | The source core to snapshot. Must have data. |
| `opts` | `object` | Options forwarded to `store.get()` for the new core. |

- Returns: [`Promise<Hypercore>`](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore) — The new static Hypercore.
- Throws: if the core has no data to staticify.

```js
const staticCore = await store.staticify(core)
```

### Watchers

#### `store.watch((core) => {})`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L278)

Register a callback called when new Hypercores are opened. `core` is the internal core for the opened Hypercore. It can be used to create weak references to a Hypercore like so:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fn` | `Function` | Callback invoked with the internal `core` each time a Hypercore is opened. |

- Returns: `void`

```js
store.watch(function (core) {
  const weakCore = new Hypercore({ core, weak: true })
})
```

#### `store.unwatch(callback)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L287)

Unregister a callback used with `store.watch(callback)` so it no longer fires.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `callback` | `Function` | The callback previously passed to `store.watch()`. |

- Returns: `void`

```js
store.unwatch(onCore)
```

### Group notifications (experimental)

#### `store.notifyGroup(topic)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L307)

Get a `handle` for updates from all `hypercore`s with the group `topic` set.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | The 32-byte group topic to watch. |

- Returns: [`GroupNotifyHandle`](/reference/helpers/corestore) — A handle that emits `update` when a core in the group changes.

```js
const handle = store.notifyGroup(topic)
handle.on('update', () => console.log('group changed'))
```

Group notifications are experimental. The API is subject to change and may break in any release.

#### `handle.update(opts = {})`

Gets updates for the `topic` the handle is for.

| Parameter | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{}` |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `since` | `0` | What timestamp to start returning updates from. Default `0` returns all updates |
| `reverse` | `true` | Flag to return updates in reverse order. Defaults to `true` so latest returned first |

```js
for await (const key of handle.updates()) {
  // ...
}
```

#### `handle.destroy()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L229)

Destroys and unregisters the `handle` from its `store`.

#### `handle.on('update', callback)`

Calls the callback whenever a core with the `topic` for the `handle` updates.

#### `store.on('group-active', (topic) => {})`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore/blob/v7.12.0/index.js#L299)

The `group-active` event emits whenever an opened Hypercore in the store updates. The `topic` is the group topic the core belongs to.

## Types

### CorestoreOptions

Options for the \{@link Corestore\} constructor. Any other options are forwarded
to the underlying `hypercore-storage` instance.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primaryKey` | [`Buffer`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | — | The 32-byte master key from which all writable named cores are derived. Generated and persisted automatically when omitted. |
| `writable` | `boolean` | `true` | Set to `false` to open the store read-only; loaded cores default to read-only too. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Open the backing storage in read-only mode. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether loaded cores are automatically attached to active replication streams. |
| `unsafe` | `boolean` | `false` | Acknowledge that passing `primaryKey` directly is unsafe; required when `primaryKey` is set on a root store. |

## Errors

Coded errors this module can throw — catch them via `err.code`.

| Error | Thrown when |
| --- | --- |
| `ASSERTION` | if `primaryKey` is set on a root store without `unsafe: true`. |

## See also

- [Work with many Hypercores using Corestore](/how-to/store-and-replicate/work-with-many-hypercores-using-corestore)—the task-oriented guide that shows how to share one store across your app.
- [Hypercore](/reference/building-blocks/hypercore)—the append-only log type Corestore opens and co-replicates.
- [Hyperbee](/reference/building-blocks/hyperbee)—commonly layered on top of named Hypercores from one store.
- [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive)—usually keeps filesystem metadata and content stores inside one shared Corestore.
- [Autobase](/reference/building-blocks/autobase)—multi-writer views often coordinate their input cores through one Corestore.
- [Hyperswarm](/reference/building-blocks/hyperswarm)—pass swarm connections to `store.replicate()` to co-replicate all managed cores over one stream.
- [Upstream Corestore repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/corestore)—source, releases, and implementation details.

/reference/helpers/localdrive/.markdown:
# Localdrive `Localdrive` exposes a local directory through an API that closely matches [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive). It is the simplest way to mirror between on-disk files and distributed drives with [Mirrordrive](/reference/helpers/mirrordrive). For upstream implementation details, see the [Localdrive repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive). ## Install ```sh npm i localdrive ``` ## Quickstart ```js import Localdrive from 'localdrive' const drive = new Localdrive('./site') await drive.put('/index.html', Buffer.from('

Hello

')) const html = await drive.get('/index.html') console.log(html?.toString()) console.log(await drive.entry('/index.html')) ``` ## API Reference ### Constructor and lifecycle #### `new Localdrive(root, [options])` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L11) Creates a drive based on a `root` directory. `root` can be relative or absolute. | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `root` | `string` | — | — | | `options` | [`LocaldriveOptions`](#localdriveoptions) | `{}` | Configuration options. | | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `followLinks` | `false` | If enabled then `entry(key)` will follow the `linkname` | | `metadata` | — | — | | `atomic` | `false` | Enable atomicity for file writing (tmp file and rename) | #### `await drive.ready()` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L22) Resolves immediately. It exists for compatibility with drive-like APIs such as [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive). - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves immediately. ```js await drive.ready() ``` #### `await drive.close()` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L25) Resolves immediately. Localdrive does not keep a background storage process open. - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves immediately. ```js await drive.close() ``` #### `await drive.flush()` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L28) Resolves immediately. It exists so code written for batched drive APIs can treat Localdrive as a drop-in target. - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves immediately. ```js await drive.flush() ``` ### Drive properties #### `drive.root` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L12) String with the resolved (absolute) drive path. - Returns: `string` #### `drive.supportsMetadata` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L14) Boolean that indicates if the drive handles or not metadata. Default `false`. - Returns: `boolean` ### Compatibility helpers #### `drive.batch()` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L32) Returns the same `Localdrive` instance. This lets batch-oriented code reuse a Localdrive target without branching. - Returns: [`Localdrive`](/reference/helpers/localdrive) — This drive instance. ```js const batch = drive.batch() await batch.put('/file.txt', Buffer.from('hello')) // on Localdrive, batch === drive ``` #### `drive.checkout()` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L36) Returns the same `Localdrive` instance. Unlike Hyperdrive, Localdrive does not expose historical versions. - Returns: [`Localdrive`](/reference/helpers/localdrive) — This drive instance. ```js const snapshot = drive.checkout() // on Localdrive, snapshot === drive ``` #### `drive.toPath(key)` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L40) Resolves a drive path such as `'/images/logo.png'` to its local filesystem path under `drive.root`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | `string` | Drive key to convert (for example `/images/logo.png`). | - Returns: `string` — Absolute filesystem path for the given key. ```js const drive = new Localdrive('/srv/data') drive.toPath('/images/logo.png') // => '/srv/data/images/logo.png' ``` ### Reading and writing entries #### `await drive.entry(name, [options])` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L46) Resolves with the entry stored at `key`, or `null` if no entry exists. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `name` | `string` | Drive key to look up (for example `/file.txt`). | | `options` | [`EntryOptions`](#entryoptions) | Entry lookup options. | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — the entry at `name` path in the drive. | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `follow` | `false` | Follow symlinks when resolving the key. | #### `await drive.get(key, [options])` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L139) Reads the file at `key` and resolves with its contents as a `Buffer`, or `null` if no file exists (also `null` for symbolic links). | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | `string` | Drive key of the file to read (for example `/blob.txt`). | | `options` | [`GetOptions`](#getoptions) | `options` are the same as in `drive.entry` method. | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — the blob at `key` path in the drive. ```js const buffer = await drive.get('/blob.txt') console.log(buffer.toString()) // => 'example' ``` #### `await drive.put(key, buffer, [options])` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L151) Creates a file at `key` path in the drive. `options` are the same as in `createWriteStream`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | `string` | Drive key of the file to write (for example `/images/logo.png`). | | `buffer` | [`Buffer\|string`](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#class-buffer) | Data to write. | | `options` | [`WriteStreamOptions`](#writestreamoptions) | — | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves when the file has been fully written and closed. ```js await drive.put('/blob.txt', Buffer.from('example')) await drive.put('/images/logo.png', Buffer.from('..'), { executable: false }) ``` #### `await drive.del(key)` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L166) Deletes the file at `key` path from the drive. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | `string` | Drive key of the file to delete (for example `/images/old-logo.png`). | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves when the file and any empty parent directories have been removed. ```js await drive.del('/images/old-logo.png') ``` #### `await drive.symlink(key, linkname)` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L191) Creates an entry in drive at `key` path that points to the entry at `linkname`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | `string` | Drive key where the symlink will be created. | | `linkname` | `string` | Target path the symlink should point to. | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves when the symlink entry has been created. ```js await drive.symlink('/images/logo.shortcut', '/images/logo.png') ``` #### `await drive.exists(name)` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L291) Resolves to `true` when `drive.entry(key)` resolves to a non-null entry, otherwise `false`. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `name` | `string` | Drive key to check (for example `/file.txt`). | - Returns: [`Promise`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Whether an entry exists at the given path. ```js const found = await drive.exists('/blob.txt') console.log(found) // => true or false ``` #### `drive.compare(entryA, entryB)` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L214) Compares two drive entries by modification time. | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `entryA` | `object` | First entry (must have an `mtime` property in milliseconds). | | `entryB` | `object` | Second entry (must have an `mtime` property in milliseconds). | - Returns: `number` — `1` if `entryA` is newer, `-1` if `entryB` is newer, and `0` if they are equal. ```js const entryA = await drive.entry('/file-a.txt') const entryB = await drive.entry('/file-b.txt') const result = drive.compare(entryA, entryB) // result: 0 (same), 1 (a is newer), or -1 (b is newer) ``` ### Listing and mirroring #### `drive.list([folder], [options])` [src](https://github.com/holepunchto/localdrive/blob/v2.2.1/index.js#L219) Returns a stream of entries for files under `folder` (defaults to the whole drive). | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `folder` | `string` | — | Unix-style path prefix to list (for example `/images`). | | `options` | [`ListOptions`](#listoptions) | `{}` | Listing options. | - Returns: `AsyncIterable

/reference/helpers/mirrordrive/.markdown:
# MirrorDrive

`Mirrordrive` computes diffs between two drive-like APIs and applies them efficiently. It is the helper that powers sync flows between [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) and [Localdrive](/reference/helpers/localdrive), including the `drive.mirror(...)` shortcut on Hyperdrive. A `MirrorDrive` instance is itself an async iterable, so iterating it with `for await (const diff of mirror)` drives the diff/copy pass and yields one diff object per entry. For source and release notes, see the [mirror-drive repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive).

## Async iteration

#### `for await (const diff of mirror)`

`MirrorDrive` is itself an async iterable. Iterating it with `for await` drives the entire diff/copy pass; each yield produces one `{ op, key, bytesRemoved, bytesAdded }` object where `op` is `'add'`, `'change'`, or `'remove'`, plus `'equal'` when `includeEquals` is set.

```js
for await (const diff of mirror) {
  console.log(diff.op, diff.key)
}
```

## Option patterns

#### `transformers`

[API definition on GitHub](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L88)
- Returns: A copy pipeline hook. Each transformer is a function `(key) => stream | null`; returning `null` skips that transform for the current file.
- Example:

```js
const mirror = new MirrorDrive(src, dst, {
  transformers: [
    (key) => key.endsWith('.txt') ? myTransformStream() : null
  ]
})
```

#### `entries`

[API definition on GitHub](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L87)
- Returns: A fixed list of entries to mirror instead of reading them from `src.list(...)`. When this option is used, `prefix` is ignored.
- Example:

```js
const entries = [{ key: '/index.html' }, { key: '/styles.css' }]
const mirror = new MirrorDrive(src, dst, { entries })
```

#### `metadataEquals`

[API definition on GitHub](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L85)
- Returns: A predicate used to decide whether metadata changes should count as a diff when both drives support metadata.
- Example:

```js
const mirror = new MirrorDrive(src, dst, {
  metadataEquals(left, right) {
    return JSON.stringify(left) === JSON.stringify(right)
  }
})
```

## Install

```sh
npm i mirror-drive
```

## Quickstart

```js
import Corestore from 'corestore'
import Hyperdrive from 'hyperdrive'
import Localdrive from 'localdrive'
import MirrorDrive from 'mirror-drive'

const store = new Corestore('./storage')
const src = new Localdrive('./site')
const dst = new Hyperdrive(store)

await dst.ready()

const mirror = new MirrorDrive(src, dst, { prune: true })

for await (const diff of mirror) {
  console.log(diff)
}
```

## API Reference

### Constructor and lifecycle

#### `new MirrorDrive(src, dst, [options])`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L72)

Creates a mirror instance to efficiently move `src` drive into `dst` drive.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | [`Hyperdrive\|Localdrive`](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) | — | Source drive to read from. |
| `dst` | [`Hyperdrive\|Localdrive`](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive) | — | Destination drive to write into (must be writable). |
| `options` | [`MirrorDriveOptions`](#mirrordriveoptions) | `{}` | Mirror options. |

#### `await mirror.done()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L131)

It starts processing all the diffing until is done.

- Returns: [`Promise<void>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) — Resolves when all diffs have been processed.

```js
const mirror = new MirrorDrive(src, dst)
await mirror.done()
console.log(mirror.count) // { files: 3, add: 2, remove: 0, change: 1 }
```

### Mirror state

#### `mirror.count`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L90)

It counts the total files proccessed, added, removed, and changed.

- Returns: `{ files: number, add: number, remove: number, change: number }`

#### `mirror.bytesAdded`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L92)

The total number of bytes copied into the destination so far.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.bytesRemoved`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L91)

The total number of bytes removed from the destination so far.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.finished`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L94)

`true` once the mirror pass has completed.

- Returns: `boolean`

#### `mirror.preloaded`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L81)

`true` once any configured preload phase has fetched the block maps it needs and estimated its download size. The blob ranges themselves may still be downloading.

- Returns: `boolean`

#### `mirror.peers`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L113)

The source drive's current peer list when `src.core` exists, otherwise an empty array.

- Returns: [`Array<object>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array)

#### `mirror.downloadProgress`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L117)

A `0..1` estimate of preload/download progress when progress tracking is enabled.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.downloadedBlocks`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L96)

The number of blob blocks downloaded from the source during the current run.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.downloadedBytes`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L98)

The number of blob bytes downloaded from the source during the current run.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.uploadedBlocks`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L101)

The number of blob blocks the source drive's blob core has uploaded to its peers during the current run.

- Returns: `number`

#### `mirror.uploadedBytes`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L102)

The number of blob bytes the source drive's blob core has uploaded to its peers during the current run.

- Returns: `number`

### Monitoring progress

#### `mirror.monitor(opts)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L124)

A monitor object that emits progress updates and exposes the latest `stats` snapshot. Requires a source drive that exposes `getBlobs`; iterating the mirror throws otherwise.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | [`MonitorOptions`](#monitoroptions) | Monitor options. |

- Returns: [`Monitor`](/reference/helpers/mirrordrive) — A new monitor instance attached to this mirror.

```js
const monitor = mirror.monitor({ interval: 500 })
monitor.on('update', (stats) => {
  console.log('downloaded', stats.download.bytes, 'bytes')
})
```

#### `monitor.stats`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L19)

- Returns: The most recent immutable stats snapshot, shaped like:
  `{
    peers,
    download: { bytes, blocks, speed, progress },
    upload: { bytes, blocks, speed }
  }`

#### `monitor.preloaded`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L25)

#### `monitor.destroyed`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L29)

- Returns: `true` after the monitor has been torn down.

#### `monitor.destroy()`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L55)

Stops update polling and detaches the monitor from the mirror.

#### `monitor.on('update', stats)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L52)

Emitted every `interval` milliseconds with the latest `monitor.stats` snapshot.

#### `monitor.on('preloaded', listener)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L187)

Emitted once preload has completed.

#### `monitor.on('destroy', listener)`

[src](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive/blob/v1.14.2/index.js#L67)

Emitted when `monitor.destroy()` runs or when the parent mirror finishes and cleans up remaining monitors.

## Types

### MirrorDriveOptions

Options for controlling how `MirrorDrive` synchronises drives.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | [`string\|Array<string>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array) | `'/'` | One or more path prefixes to mirror. When an array, each prefix is mirrored in order. |
| `dryRun` | `boolean` | `false` | Walk the diff and emit events without writing any changes to `dst`. |
| `prune` | `boolean` | `true` | Remove files from `dst` that no longer exist in `src`. |
| `includeEquals` | `boolean` | `false` | Emit `{ op: 'equal' }` events for files that are identical in both drives. |
| `filter` | `function(string): boolean` | — | Called with each source key; return `false` to skip that entry. |
| `metadataEquals` | `function(*,*): boolean` | — | Custom equality check for file metadata; receives `(srcMetadata, dstMetadata)`. |
| `batch` | `boolean` | `false` | Accumulate destination writes in a single batch and flush at the end. |
| `entries` | [`Array<object>\|null`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array) | `null` | Pre-computed list of source entries to mirror; when provided, `prefix` is ignored. |
| `ignore` | [`string\|Array<string>\|function`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array) | — | Paths to exclude from both drives' listings; ignored paths in `dst` are therefore never pruned. |
| `transformers` | [`Array<function>`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array) | `[]` | Array of factory functions `(key) => stream \| null`; each returned stream is piped between source read and destination write. |
| `progress` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable download/upload progress tracking (requires `src.getBlobs`). |
| `dedup` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable content-addressed deduplication using Rabin chunking on the destination. |

### MonitorOptions

Options for the `monitor()` method.

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interval` | `number` | `250` | How often (in milliseconds) the monitor emits `update` events with fresh stats. |

## See also

- [Create a full peer-to-peer filesystem with Hyperdrive](/how-to/stream-and-share-media/create-a-full-peer-to-peer-filesystem-with-hyperdrive)—end-to-end workflow that mirrors between Localdrive and Hyperdrive.
- [Hyperdrive](/reference/building-blocks/hyperdrive)—exposes `drive.mirror(...)` and is the canonical distributed destination/source for Mirrordrive.
- [Localdrive](/reference/helpers/localdrive)—the local filesystem companion API most often paired with Mirrordrive.
- [Drives](/reference/tools/drives)—CLI tool whose `drives mirror` command is powered by the same sync logic.
- [Upstream mirror-drive repository](https://github.com/holepunchto/mirror-drive)—source, releases, and implementation details.
